hook: Motivation is the worst reason to start working. Here's what to use instead.
body:
**Motivation is the worst reason to start working. Here's what to use instead.**

Motivation is an emotional state. Like all emotional states, it is temporary, unpredictable, and completely outside your direct control. Building a work system on top of motivation is like building a schedule that only functions when the weather is good.

Here's what high-output people actually use: behaviour triggers. A trigger is a fixed external condition that initiates a fixed action — no motivation required, no internal state assessment, no negotiation. You sit in the chair, you open the document. Not because you feel like it. Because the chair and the document are the trigger sequence, and you've run it often enough that the behaviour is nearly automatic.

Waiting to feel motivated is itself a form of procrastination. It is the most socially acceptable one, because it sounds responsible — "I'll work when I'm in the right headspace." You won't. The headspace follows the work. It never precedes it.

The reframe: you don't need to feel ready to start. You need a trigger condition that makes starting the default response, regardless of how you feel.

One action: design a two-step pre-work ritual — same chair, same first action, every time. Not because it's pleasant. Because repetition builds automaticity, and automaticity doesn't need motivation.

Full trigger system in the link in bio.
